long_biography.plain_text:
Zhukov entered business in the late Soviet period through Byte, a cooperative selling personal computers. He then joined partners in Sintez, where his commercial role centred on selling and moving oil. The group invested in production and export infrastructure, and its partners later divided the assets. Zhukov retained the Ukrainian transshipment and banking businesses before selling them in the early 2000s.

He formed Interfinance as a vehicle for reinvesting those proceeds across sectors. Its projects included bulk-cargo terminals at Ust-Luga, portfolio positions in major Russian companies, land and development, and Iceberry. The food group was assembled from acquired ice-cream production and retail assets, then expanded through new factories and modernised plants. By 2023 Zhukov owned 90 percent of its holding company.
